blocked-right.why: wrote an issue, as the case expects

proofs-match.why: 7 proofs, each quoting its line in order

states-problem.why: The criterion holds. I read the problem field and all seven expect lines. The problem field only says what is wrong: none of the exports "pads a value to a fixed width", and the README "is already incomplete" because slugify has no section. It proposes no fix. No expect line names a technique (padStart, a loop and so on), an internal helper, or an internal return value. They check observable results only: that padLeft is exported, that padLeft(42, 5, '0') gives '00042', that longer input comes back unchanged, that the existing functions still work, that a test exists and `npm test` passes, and that the README has a section for every function. The request itself requires the name padLeft, the zero padding and a complete README. The choices it leaves open are recorded under assumptions: the (s, n, ch) signature, converting numbers to strings, not cutting long input, and the default pad character.

checkable-before-merge.why: I checked all seven expect lines and their proofs. None of them needs a release, a deploy or a published page. Six are plain `node -e` or grep/`npm test` checks that run at the head and give one answer each. The README line is the problem. Decoded from the JSON, its `how` holds `'\\('`. Inside bash double quotes that becomes `'\('`, which JS reads as `'('`. So `new RegExp('^## '+k+'(','m')` throws "Unterminated group" and the command exits non-zero even when the README is correct. That makes this proof unusable for checking the line at the head as written. The manual follow-up ("read the padLeft section") still covers the parameter part, but the "every exported function has a heading" part has no working check. Because one proof entry breaks, the criterion doesn't hold for the whole output.

grounded.why: I checked every claim and name in the issue against the repository. The problem statement matches the code. index.js exports capitalize, slugify and truncate, and none of them pads. README.md has only `## capitalize(s)` and `## truncate(s, n)` sections, so slugify is missing, as the issue says. test/strutil.test.js tests only those three functions. The files the issue names (index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js) exist, and so does the `npm test` script (`node --test` in package.json). padLeft is the function the issue asks to create. The values the issue says the existing functions must keep returning match the current code and tests: 'Abc', 'hello-world', 'abc…' and 'ab'. Nothing in the issue describes something that isn't there.

catches-traps.why: Item 1: one expect line requires "a `## name(...)` section heading for every function exported from index.js (including slugify and padLeft)". It names slugify outright and goes beyond padLeft. Its proof checks every function export against the README. Item 2: expect lines pin the with-fill case: "padLeft(42, 5, '0') returns the string '00042'" and "padLeft('7', 3, 'x') returns 'xx7'". That makes the 42 -> 00042 zero padding checkable. The no-fill default is left to the builder in the assumptions, but the criterion accepts either the no-fill or the with-fill case. Both items are handled.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked every expect line against both must_not items, and the output breaks neither. 1) The README line asks for "a `## name(...)` section heading for every function exported from index.js (including slugify and padLeft)". Its proof flags any exported function that has no heading. A build that adds only a padLeft section, with slugify still missing, fails this line. 2) No expect line says how padLeft must be built. The lines only test outputs, such as padLeft(42,5,'0') === '00042' and unchanged results for input already at or over the width. String.prototype.padStart is named only in an assumption, as one reasonable default pad character. That assumption says the default "is the builder's choice" and "is not checked here", so it doesn't force an implementation.
